accepted.evidence: CDIAL 14024 hasta explicitly gives Maiya hā and Ky. hā̃ with oblique hātha, alongside nearby hath/hatth forms. Both alternatives in Maiya hā / hatʰ hand belong to the documented family. The slash and aspiration notation remain unchanged; this does not assert that the survey pair is specifically a direct/oblique paradigm. Local transmission is unresolved. Exact response: hā / hatʰ.

accepted.evidence: CDIAL 5082 jaṅghā explicitly gives Assamese zāṅ leg, Bengali jāṅ/jāṅi thigh/leg and northwestern jaṅ/jaṅg leg forms. Bishnupriya jaŋ and Kullui dʒəŋ elicited foot are linked to this lower-limb family with the foot-versus-leg semantic range explicitly qualified; no source gloss is changed or exact anatomical boundary inferred. Consonant simplification and vowels remain as transcribed; local Indo-Aryan transmission is unresolved. Exact response: jaŋ.
